references.context: Logic and notation: Iverson bracket [P] returns numeric 1 when proposition P is true and 0 otherwise. In the Kronecker delta definition P is the equality predicate a=b on Γ; the general Iverson notation applies to arbitrary propositions, not merely to equality.
references.reason: The general Iverson bracket is an independently reusable indicator construction for propositions, whereas the current numerical delta specializes it to equality on Γ.
references.matching_note: Independent meaning inventory has no general Iverson-indicator formulation; do not identify the general indicator of arbitrary P with the particular Kronecker equality delta.

references.disposition: The underlying equality predicate has no new mathematical structure.

references.disposition: Having one endpoint in A and the other in B is precisely the defining crossing-edge restriction for the bipartite partition in this formulation. The bipartition condition does not require nonempty vertex parts.

references.disposition: The existence of one threshold N_ε depending on ε but independent of every x in D is the quantified defining condition of uniform convergence in this source. The metric uniform convergence specialization is already linked; an additional threshold-construction meaning would not be distinct and could cause recursive explanation. This is strictly stronger than a pointwise threshold that may depend on x.
This is strictly stronger than pointwise convergence except in special cases.

references.phrase: pairwise independence of events A and B
references.matching_note: The independent-events meaning exactly defines P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) for each pair of measurable events, including zero-probability cases. The present sigma-algebra definition universally requires that condition for every A∈G₁ and B∈G₂, rather than only one selected pair.

references.disposition: Requires all event pairs, not existence of some independent pair.
